transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, this is Brett. Account number and PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, hi. Yes, it's 5561-209-847, and the PIN is 3318. My name's Walter Hughes.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay. What's the issue?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So, about five weeks ago I upgraded to the 500 megabit plan, because we've got the kids doing school stuff online and my wife and I both work from home a couple of days a week. And I'm not getting anywhere near that. Every time I test it, it's about fifty or sixty.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And it's not just the number, our video calls freeze, the kids' streaming buffers. It's honestly worse than before we upgraded, which makes no sense to me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello? Are you there?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yeah. I'm looking at the account. It says you're on the 500 plan.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's what I'm saying. I'm paying for the 500 and I'm getting fifty.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And when I upgraded, the guy on the phone said we'd get at least three hundred on WiFi, easily. He was very clear about that. That's the whole reason I upgraded.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can't comment on what sales told you. I'm technical support.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, but he was from S-Net, same as you. I'm not making it up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm not saying you're making it up. I just can't see what was said on a sales call.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fine. I've been with you eleven years, you know. We've never had a problem like this.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay. Read me the serial number on the bottom of the router.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hang on, I need to tip it over. Okay. It's S N, 4, 4, 0, 9, B, 7, 7, 2, 1.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, that matches what's on the account.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay. I'm going to send a refresh to the modem. It'll restart.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay. I did restart it myself this morning, for what it's worth.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well, I'm sending it from here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Alright. The lights have all gone off.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is something supposed to be happening? The lights are flashing now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's rebooting. It takes a few minutes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, the lights look normal again. The globe is white.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is it working now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I just ran the test again on my laptop. It says 54 down.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Like I said, the refresh takes time to settle. You'll need to test it again later.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You didn't say that. You said it would restart.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It needs time to settle after the refresh. That's normal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How long is later? An hour? Tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could be a few hours.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, well, can you stay on while I test it again in a few minutes? I'd rather not have to call back in.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can test it now if you want.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay. Testing again... 58 down. 11 up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a bit better.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's four megabits better. That's nothing.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It'll keep improving as it settles.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You said that already. I don't see how restarting it from your end is any different from me restarting it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It resets the connection profile on our side.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And has that ever fixed a problem like this? Fifty instead of five hundred?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Sometimes. Hold on.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello? Brett?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yeah. I was checking the line again. The line's fine.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Look, I've been paying for the 500 for over a month and getting about a tenth of it. And I've been paying twenty more a month for it. That's really not okay.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Speeds aren't guaranteed. It says up to 500 on the plan.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Up to 500, sure, but fifty? That's not up to, that's nowhere near it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The line is showing 500 provisioned. So the line is fine.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Then why am I getting fifty?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Probably the WiFi. WiFi is your own setup.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's your router. You sent it to me when I upgraded.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The router's showing online. It's fine.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Online isn't the same as fast. I'm sitting in the kitchen, it's maybe five metres from the router, there's one wall. My wife's laptop is the same, and the kids' tablets. It's slow on all of them.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So is there anything you can actually check? Anything at all?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I sent the refresh. You should have restarted the router before you called, that's the first thing anyone should do.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I did restart it. I told you that. I restarted it this morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well, the refresh from our side is different.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay. Fine. Can I at least get some money back for the five weeks? I've been paying for a speed I'm not getting.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's not something I handle. That's a billing team thing. You'd have to call back and ask them.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can't you just transfer me?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The billing line closes at six. You'd have to call back tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So I've been on the phone with you for ten minutes, nothing's changed, and now I have to call back tomorrow and start again with somebody else.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Billing is a different department.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can I speak to a supervisor, please?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A supervisor's going to tell you the same thing. There's nothing I can do about WiFi speeds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'd still like to speak to one.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: They're all busy at the moment. You'd have to wait a long time.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Unbelievable. Okay. So what am I supposed to do about the speed? Just live with it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously if you want the full 500 you plug the laptop into the router with a cable. That's basic stuff. WiFi is never going to give you the full speed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I don't need the full 500 on WiFi. I'd be happy with two hundred. Before the upgrade we were getting about a hundred and fifty on WiFi, on the old router. Now it's fifty.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Different routers perform differently.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: A friend of mine said it might be the WiFi channel, that if everyone on our street is on the same channel it slows down. Can you change that from your end?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can change the channel in the router settings yourself. There's a guide on the website.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I wouldn't know where to start with that. Can you walk me through it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's in the guide. It's step by step. It's not difficult.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm sure it's not difficult for you. I'm asking for help, that's why I called technical support.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The guide covers it. Go to the website, search WiFi channel, and follow the steps.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay. Fine. I'll try that later.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So the new router is worse than the old one? Can you send me a different one?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can't send equipment unless there's a fault. The router's showing no fault.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: But it's slower than the old one. Isn't that a fault?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not on our system, no. It's online.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay. Is there an engineer who can come out and look at it, then?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: An engineer visit is for line faults. The line is fine. If they come out and it's your WiFi, there's a call-out charge.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How much is that?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Sixty-five.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So I pay sixty-five for you to tell me it's my WiFi. On the router you sent me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If it's not a line fault, yes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fine. Forget it. I'll call billing tomorrow and I'll ask them about cancelling, honestly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: They can help with that.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great. Is there a reference number or anything for this call, so I don't have to explain it all again?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's on the account.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right. Is there a reference number, though?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: They'll see the call on the account.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Then can you at least put a note on there that I've complained about the speed, and that I asked for a supervisor and didn't get one? I want that written down.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can add a note.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What will it say?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Customer called about WiFi speed. Refresh sent.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's not what I said. I said I'm getting fifty on a five hundred plan, on your router, for five weeks, and I want a refund and a supervisor. Please put that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay. I'll put customer reports slow speed and wants a refund.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And the supervisor.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And requested a supervisor.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My son has an online exam tomorrow morning, you know. If it freezes during that, I don't know what we'll do.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can plug his computer into the router with a cable.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: He's upstairs. The router is downstairs. There's no cable that goes that far.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Then he'll be on WiFi.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fine.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No. Clearly not.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay. Thanks for calling. Bye.
